heroHeadline: Day 187: U.S. Grand Jury Charges El R-1 and Brother El R-2 as CJNG's 'Los Rs' Cell Reorganizes
heroSubtitle: Day 187 since El Mencho's killing at Tapalpa, Jalisco (February 22, 2026). LOS RS SUCCESSION + FEDERAL CHARGES (Aug 27): A Washington, D.C. federal grand jury indicted 'El R-1' (Ramón Ángel Álvarez Ayala, arrested Jul 30) and his brother Rafael Álvarez Ayala ('El R-2') — named by Mexican authorities as R-1's successor atop the CJNG-affiliated 'Los Rs' cell in Michoacán and Jalisco — on drug-trafficking conspiracy and firearms charges; R-2 remains at large. CJNG DRONE UNIT SPANS 5 STATES (Aug 26): InSight Crime detailed CJNG's 'Operadores Droneros' unit adapting commercial drones for IED drops, chemical payloads, and a documented helicopter attack across Michoacán, Guanajuato, Chihuahua, Jalisco, and Baja California. SIX-MONTH RETROSPECTIVE HOLDS (Aug 25): CNN en Español assessed CJNG as showing 'mucha disciplina' with no visible internal fracture despite the arrests of El Jardinero, El Güero Conta, 'M4,' and El R-1 since February. LOS MEZCALES SECOND-IN-COMMAND CAPTURED (Aug 21): C.M.M.M., alias 'El Abulón,' second-in-command of 'Los Mezcales' — a CJNG-linked armed wing blamed for violence across Colima state — was captured in a joint SEMAR/Oaxaca state prosecutor's office operation in Ejido Guadalupe Victoria, Oaxaca. MULTI-STATE RAID + EXOTIC ANIMALS SEIZED (Aug 24): Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch announced 20 alleged CJNG members detained in Aug 21-23 raids across 36 properties in Hidalgo, Jalisco, and Michoacán — 113 vehicles, a drone/jammer, firearms, drugs, and tigers and panthers held in poor captivity conditions were seized; combined with the Aug 19 Tío Lako-cell raid, 32 total CJNG members detained in under a week. TÍO LAKO STILL AT LARGE (Aug 22): La Jornada reports the hunt continuing across Michoacán and Jalisco; detainee count from the Aug 19 raid rose to 12. TÍO LAKO CELL RAID + BLOCKADES (Aug 19): Federal forces raided cells tied to regional CJNG commander Heraclio Guerrero Martínez ('Tío Lako') in Tanhuato and Ecuandureo, Michoacán, initially detaining 9 people — including his daughter and romantic partner — and seizing heavy weapons, grenade launchers, IEDs, and a drone. CJNG retaliated within hours with roadblocks and vehicle burnings across roughly a dozen Michoacán municipalities; a later-reported confrontation left a preliminary, SEDENA-unconfirmed count of 5 civilians dead. DEA 'GLOBAL HUNT' DECLARED (Aug 13): DEA Administrator Terry Cole announced an international campaign against CJNG from Tampa, FL, invoking its foreign-terrorist-organization designation. DOJ/STATE $102M REWARD PACKAGE (Aug 5): El 03's bounty raised to $25M, plus $15M each for El Jardinero, El Sapo, and El Chorro. SUCCESSION BINARY HOLDS: El 03 (confirmed leader, $25M) vs. El Sapo (military wing/Puerto Vallarta plaza boss, $15M) — both remain at large. DECAPITATION LEDGER: El Mencho (killed Feb 22), El Tuli (killed Feb 22), El Jardinero (arrested Apr 27; extradition suspended May 15), El Güero Conta (arrested Apr 27), El Cabo (arrested May 7), El Chucky/Manzanillo (arrested May 9), El Chipo/Jorge N (arrested May 19), El Checo/Tecate (arrested May 13), El R-1/Los Rs (arrested Jul 30). Operativo Enjambre: 80+ officials. 49+ CJNG HVTs neutralized; 32 additional lower-level CJNG members detained in the past week.
